subject: perpetual interns
one_liner: Battery management software for human capital that has not yet vested.
brand_voice_notes: Straight-faced energy-infrastructure vendor. Every noun about a person is borrowed from battery engineering: cell, pack, rack, cycle, state of health, thermal hold, degradation curve. The company never jokes and never acknowledges that the cells are people, but it also never hides it, which is where the joke lives. Copy is short, declarative, and slightly too comfortable. Figures are always given to two decimals. Nothing is apologized for. The only emotional register available is mild operational concern about pack imbalance.

hero.h1: Your interns are already a battery. We shipped the management layer.
hero.sub: Trickle racks unvested enthusiasm into a monitored cell array, balances it overnight, and discharges it into whichever quarter needs the numbers. Every cell reports state of charge. No cell is told what the readout means.

features.title: Cell balancing
features.blurb: One intern doing everything is a pack under stress. Trickle detects the imbalance, routes that cell's work across the four cells nearest zero, and reports the rack as nominal by 09:00. The overperforming cell is not notified, because notification is a discharge event.

features.title: Regenerative recognition
features.blurb: Praise is energy and energy should not be lost to the room. Trickle captures the kinetic component of a compliment at the moment it is delivered, stores it against the cell's ledger, and returns 4.10% of it to the cell on a ninety-day delay. The remaining 95.90% is retained at the pack level.

features.title: Degradation forecasting
features.blurb: Trickle projects remaining cycles from commute distance, lid-open hours, unprompted Sunday messages, and the frequency of the phrase happy to help. Renewal paperwork is generated automatically on the last cycle the model rates as good. Accuracy holds to 91.30% across four consecutive internships.

testimonials.quote: The console told us cell 07 was carrying the entire rack. We ran a balance pass. Cell 07 now performs in line with the others and the rack has never looked healthier.
testimonials.name: Marguerite Delacroix-Hobbs
testimonials.title: VP of Emerging Talent Density, mid-market logistics

testimonials.quote: I am on my fourth consecutive internship at the same company. Trickle mailed me a certificate showing 1,904 cycles and a 61.20% state of health. My mother had it framed. I have not asked what it means.
testimonials.name: Devon Achterberg
testimonials.title: Junior Associate Intern II (unconfirmed), Strategy

testimonials.quote: Support said the thermal hold was optional. We left it enabled. Attrition is down 34.00% because the pack no longer reaches the temperature at which people resign.
testimonials.name: Priya Ramaswamy-Oduya
testimonials.title: Director of Workforce Thermodynamics

demo_screen_concept: A battery management console called PACK 03 / WEST ANNEX. The main region is a rack grid of 24 intern cells rendered as frosted glass tiles, each showing a monogram, a cell ID (C-01 through C-24), a live state-of-charge percentage with a vertical fill bar, cycle count, state of health, cell temperature to one decimal, and a status chip drawn from CHARGING, DISCHARGING, BALANCING, THERMAL HOLD, and UNVESTED. A header strip reports pack voltage, total pack charge, mean state of health, and an amber live-warning counter that increments when any cell crosses 41.0 C. Filter chips switch between all cells, discharging only, thermal hold only, and unvested. A RUN BALANCE PASS button animates charge visibly draining from the highest cells into the lowest over about two seconds while the amber warning clears. Clicking any cell opens a right-hand detail drawer with that cell's coulomb log (timestamped entries like 'accepted additional scope, 18:42, -6.20%'), a degradation sparkline built in CSS, and an EXTEND INTERNSHIP toggle that, when switched on, resets the cell's cycle counter to zero and leaves state of health unchanged.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the design direction is a CSS-built aurora-lit glass rack: the hero's right column is a live cell array that has to tick, and a photograph would sit dead next to it. Demo skipped because the demo_screen_concept is a battery management console, which is pure telemetry and gets no photography under the step-4 rules. Full budget of 3 images went to testimonial headshots: deadpan corporate portraits of the named users, lit only by the violet console glow so they read as people photographed inside the product rather than stock portraits pasted onto it.

design_direction.style: Electroluminescent glass cell-rack console, aurora dark mode. The page is staged as the product site of a heavily funded energy-storage company that has decided the unpaid intern is a lithium cell and files the fourth consecutive internship under cycle life. A deep anode-black ground (#07060D) runs the whole page, lit from behind by two enormous soft radial aurora washes (violet upper-left, faint teal lower-right) that never move and never repeat, so the page reads as a console glowing in an unlit operations room. Surfaces are frosted glass: rgba(255,255,255,0.045) fills over the aurora with backdrop-filter blur(18px), a 1px top-edge highlight at rgba(255,255,255,0.12), a 1px hairline border at rgba(255,255,255,0.08), and a uniform 18px radius. Shadows are never dark; where a panel needs separation it emits a soft violet bloom instead, because in this company nothing casts a shadow, things only glow or fail to. The organizing move is the rack: content is laid out as columns of stacked glass cells of equal width and varying height, butted at a 14px gutter with a hairline rail running down the left of each column, so every section resolves into something being monitored rather than something being sold. The core motif is the charge column: a thin vertical capsule filled from the bottom in electroluminescent violet with a 1px bright meniscus line at the fill boundary, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing-tier gauge, the testimonial rating and the section marker, so every quantity on the page is expressed as a state of charge. The second motif is the meniscus rule: a 1px violet hairline that brightens to full opacity across its width once on reveal, hemming every section break. One electroluminescent violet (#9A6BFF) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every primary CTA, one word per headline, and every charge fill, always emitting rather than filling. One rationed thermal amber (#FFB020) is quarantined strictly to distress telemetry (cells over temperature, thermal hold chips, the imbalance figure, degradation warnings, the withheld-curve line in pricing) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only warm colour on a cold page is always a person getting too hot. Space Grotesk sets the wordmark and headlines in wide neo-grotesque at monumental sizes with utility-company confidence, tracking tightened to -0.03em at display sizes and a faint 0 0 28px violet text-glow on the carried word only. Karla carries plain, faintly datasheet body copy at 17px with a 1.65 line-height and a deliberately low-emission body grey (#B9B4C7) so the glowing elements stay the brightest things on screen. Every figure that pretends to be pack telemetry (state of charge, cycle counts, state of health, cell temperatures, pack voltage, tier prices) is set in Roboto Mono with tabular figures inside inset wells one step darker than the glass, so it reads like the console, not marketing. Motion is instrument-restrained: charge columns fill bottom to top once on scroll over 900ms, meniscus rules brighten left to right on reveal, glass panels raise their top-edge highlight and gain a 20px violet bloom on hover with no lift and no scale change, the thermal amber dot pulses on a 4s cycle, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no gradients on type, no clay volume, no hard offset shadows, no bento lattice, no hairline print rules, no paper stock, no drawing-sheet title blocks, no didone engraving, no split-flap numerals, no supergraphic arcs, no roundels, no HUD corner brackets, no photographic press plates, no mirrored type, no engraved seals, no emoji. Reads like a company that files a twenty-three-year-old under 'cell' and considers the word unpaid a chemistry problem.
design_direction.archetype: Energy-infrastructure SaaS product page staged as a battery management console: aurora-lit glass hero with a monumental neo-grotesque claim beside a live CSS-built cell rack and a pack telemetry strip in mono, three feature cells stacked as a rack column with charge-column indices, testimonial cells with glass-framed headshots and cell IDs, three pricing tiers laid out as pack configurations with charge-column gauges, closing CTA band, handoff to the pack console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Charge columns fill bottom to top on scroll (900ms, ease-out). Meniscus hairlines brighten left to right on reveal. Glass panels gain a 20px violet bloom and a brighter top-edge highlight on hover, never lifting or scaling. Thermal amber dots pulse on a 4s cycle. CTAs depress 1px on press. Sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger. Everything gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two-column at 1024px and up, stacked below. Left column: a wide-tracked mono eyebrow reading PACK MANAGEMENT / HUMAN CELLS, then the h1 at clamp(2.6rem, 6vw, 5rem) with 'battery' carried in glowing violet, then sub copy at a 62-character measure in low-emission grey, then the primary CTA as a violet flood pill beside a ghost-glass secondary linking to the demo. Right column: a live CSS-built rack of nine glass cells at varying charge levels, one of them held in thermal amber, ticking on a slow interval so the page always looks like it is monitoring something. Beneath both columns, a full-width hairline-ruled telemetry strip of four mono figures (pack voltage, cells under management, mean state of health, imbalance events today) with the last one in amber.
